children: India's top court on Thursday dismissed the market regulator's case against the National Stock Exchange of India (NSEI.NS), over allegations of unfair access to the bourse's systems, the exchange said on Friday.
The Supreme Court dismissed the case after the regulator agreed in-principle to settle the allegations, NSE said. The exchange had said in July that it would pay $155 million to settle the case.
The dismissal marks the end of a decade-long regulatory dispute and removes the biggest legal overhang for the exchange as it prepares for ​an initial public offering later ​this ⁠year.

NSE filed draft offer documents for its listing in June and has been doing investor ​roadshows for what is expected to be one of India's two mega IPOs this ⁠year, ​alongside billionaire Mukesh ​Ambani's Reliance Jio.

In 2019, the Securities and Exchange Board of India passed two orders against the exchange, alleging it did not exercise due diligence while setting a network that allowed some high-frequency traders unfair access to its network servers.
In 2023, NSE received relief from the Securities Appellate Tribunal, prompting the regulator to appeal to the Supreme Court.
